Squirrel package and installed-version identity

Run the exact root entrypoint build-installer.bat /s. It builds the real desktop payload and produces unsigned Squirrel.Windows Setup.exe, RELEASES, and MaterialBuildroot-<version>-full.nupkg. The output receipt binds the files to the unchanged source commit, tree, index, manifest, lockfile, and effective installed version. Packaging checks the actual application archive metadata against that version. Production does not install or launch the application and does not establish update, rollback, or runtime acceptance.

Every normal installer production calls assemblePayloads with complete: true and packages every required bundled payload through extraResources. That option requires completeness of the explicit bundled inventory; it does not claim every registered external tool is available offline. The real installed consumer already resolves resources/offline-payloads/manifest.json before user-selected tool receipts, with original companion files and notices retained. The package producer requires the assembled manifest hash and notice file in the unpacked package, and records explicit bundled scope, external-tool states, source and license metadata in the source-bound receipt. A directory development build remains explicitly core-only and does not claim bundled-tool completeness.

Host-selected tools remain explicit

The manifest and receipt use scope: bundled-payload-inventory, bundledComplete, requiredBundledToolIds, and wholeToolsetOffline: false. The existing ten pinned bundled tools remain required. externalTools separately describes vboxmanage, vmrun, qemu-img, and ssh as externally installed and user-admitted capabilities. These rows carry purpose/acquisition/licensing boundaries, availability: not-evaluated-during-build, admission: required-at-runtime, admissionReceipt: not-present-in-package, installation: not-performed-by-assembly, and runtimeVerified: false. Their provenance names the host-native picker and local user-data receipt scope, with neither a receipt nor executable path included in the package. A bundle row is not an external admission receipt, and an external declaration is not an installed executable.

No hypervisor, image converter, or SSH installation, license acceptance, elevation, PATH discovery, or executable probe occurs during payload assembly. Their host-selected routes stay unavailable until the normal native selection, consent and integrity admission succeeds. Required bundled payloads retain their original archives, notices and hashes; any registered tool missing from both explicit classifications still stops production. See offline payload boundaries for the actual source and license conditions.

The FFmpeg transcoder profile keeps the pinned original archive identity, selected ffmpeg.exe, and all original non-executable documentation and notices. Its explicit source inventory accounts for 43 retained members (117,097,063 uncompressed bytes) and two excluded companion executables, ffplay.exe and ffprobe.exe (212,124,672 uncompressed bytes). This profile does not claim their playback or probe capabilities. Package receipts retain the profile, composition, excluded-member identities and source inventory alongside the generated manifest hash. These are actual source selection figures, not a produced installer-size measurement or permission to change the delivery cap.

Hosted preservation run 38970438575 at bc5531d7b5c3c9fbf0c6da84a3f6c5b490ad25cf initialized installed MSVC 18.10 and produced the 274-module renderer, then exited 1 because the earlier assembler treated these four newly registered external tools as missing bundled payloads. Native broker and embedding-helper compilation had not run. The explicit classification correction does not upgrade that failed run into compilation or packaging evidence; a new exact-source production remains required.

Use --payload-cache <absolute-directory> to reuse previously acquired immutable archives. Only registry-named archive files are copied into the producer's own ignored cache. Source caches remain read only, and assembly revalidates every pinned archive before extraction. No absolute cache path enters publication metadata. Each produced release asset is measured and must fit the 1.4 GB transfer budget; oversized output is retained as incomplete production rather than being renamed or misrepresented.

Installer production uses an exclusively created short directory under the current writable temporary directory because the genuine NuGet packaging tool retains legacy path-length limits. A private ownership receipt records source and ownership there; its path and receipt are excluded from public output. The producer checks the deepest assembled path against its packaging budget before launching NuGet. Failed staging is retained. Activation still verifies the complete source-bound output; a cross-volume activation copies the verified output while retaining the original producer tree. This changes no host path-limit setting and substitutes no packaging tool.

Native broker resource

Normal desktop installer production initializes the verified installed MSVC x64 and Windows SDK route through the root entrypoint, then calls scripts/build/native-file-broker.ps1 inside the same source-bound production. The generated executable and its matching SHA-256 manifest are appended as resources/native-file-broker/material-file-broker.exe and resources/native-file-broker/broker-manifest.json, alongside the complete offline tool resource. The object file is not packaged. The producer checks the compiled identity again after packaging and records only toolchain versions and hashes, without compiler or machine paths.

A missing supported installed compiler or SDK stops the root entrypoint honestly. This path performs no local toolchain installation, license acceptance, elevation, or host setting change. Hosted production can use its verified existing compiler installation. A compiled broker remains runtimeVerified: false; packaging alone does not admit external adapters or establish isolation, cancellation, or output-publication runtime acceptance. Development directory builds remain explicitly without a produced broker unless a separate supported production supplies one.

Separate flashing helper production

A later installer candidate also calls the flashing owner's Invoke-FlashingBuild API from scripts/build/flashing.ps1 through the root producer. The helper acquires only pinned official .NET SDK 8.0.426 and runtime 8.0.32 inputs into its owned cache when production actually runs, uses the exact project/global runtime pins, and publishes self-contained win-x64 output. This is a build-time portable input route, with no machine-wide .NET installation or helper/device execution. The fixed function call receives paths as process-environment argument values rather than interpolated shell source.

The whole produced output and original .NET notices are included at resources/native/flashing/, alongside the existing broker and offline tools. Admission requires the exact executable hash, protocol/version/source manifest, all four notice files, and explicit DebugType=None/DebugSymbols=false; any .pdb or .mdb output is retained but rejected from packaging. The package receipt records the pins, source hashes and runtimeVerified: false, and rechecks the executable, manifest and notices after packaging. No self-contained output size or native consent/runtime acceptance is inferred from this source integration. It is separate from the frozen 714cd3d embedding-observer diagnostic and must receive its own later exact-source production evidence.

Genuine setup embedding and admission

The genuine helper source is retained unchanged in native/squirrel-writezip/, with its original MIT notice and byte/hash provenance from official Squirrel.Windows revision eef37460aef77b2f9de8cd2237c1e55b344a6554 (tag 2.0.1). The root producer compiles that source for x64 using the same verified installed compiler route. Through the supported customSquirrelVendorDir option it copies the pinned genuine vendor inventory, retains the rebuilt helper as WriteZipToSetup.Genuine.exe, and places a bounded invocation observer at the official WriteZipToSetup.exe command path. The observer forwards only the documented resource-copy and ZIP-embedding forms to the genuine sibling through CreateProcessW without a shell. It does not introduce a custom self-extracting format, patch an executable, alter the setup template, or claim a compiler result as installation proof.

This route addresses a concrete packaging boundary: the pinned vendor helper is a 32-bit executable without large-address awareness, while its official source reads the entire embedded ZIP into memory before the resource update. The retained large-payload run produced a setup containing only its template updater. The official 2.0.1 source logs and continues after an embedding-helper failure. The original helper's exact failure and any before/after resource-edit transition were not captured, so an address-space limit remains a hypothesis rather than a proven cause. A successful future x64 production must establish the actual embedding outcome.

Before production can succeed, squirrel-setup.cjs reads the actual configured setup's PE resource tree and embedded ZIP directory. It requires the exact current full-package filename, a single-record RELEASES, and the genuine updater, rejects missing, duplicate, encrypted, escaping or unsupported members, and streams the embedded contents to compare sizes and SHA-256 identities. The embedded feed's SHA-1 and size must match that same full package. The resulting receipt records member identities and byte counts without machine paths. An MZ signature or filename alone never establishes a complete offline installer. Post-packaging resource editing remains enabled; preservation of the complete payload must pass actual admission.

The retained complete-payload run from source bd0a4fce58cc69cd9ec19b30ba86a9ec7d166720 assembled ten tools, 30,972 files and 3,760,387,226 uncompressed bytes, then produced a 1,450,598,556-byte full package and 1,392,019,114-byte delta. Its root entrypoint exited 1 because the full package exceeded the unchanged 1.4 GB budget. Its 228,864-byte configured setup embedded only a 35,682-byte ZIP containing a 69,120-byte template updater, with no full package or feed. The output was retained and never activated or published. That run is failure evidence, not complete offline installer acceptance. The new x64 helper, embedding admission, native broker production and any subsequent size repair remain unverified until their actual source-bound production runs.

Hosted preservation production

The existing Windows release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) accepts a manual execution_target of windows-2025 or windows-2022; the preferred current target is windows-2025. It bootstraps the pinned publication CLI and invokes the exact root build-installer.bat /s with the source-bound workflow identity. The root entrypoint discovers the verified installed MSVC x64/SDK route, compiles the native broker and genuine x64 embedding helper, acquires all complete declared payloads and a compatible previous baseline, and applies the unchanged 1.4 GB delivery admission. No local compiler installation is required or silently attempted.

Publication has a separate exact-source eligibility step. A source not contained in freshly fetched main produces eligible=false and skips release publication; unavailable ancestry fails admission rather than granting it. A failed production step also prevents publication. Preservation of a task branch does not itself establish release eligibility. The workflow's existing always() collection and nonmasking upload retain diagnostic evidence without turning the original failure into success.

The producer leaves an ignored local pointer to its exact short staging and an original private ownership receipt in that staging. The collector checks source, owning checkout, direct temporary-child identity and absence of linked ancestors, without scanning global temporary directories. It retains only a sanitized ownership projection, compiled helper identities, known output filenames/sizes/hashes, and the setup PE/ZIP member receipt. Original paths and the private receipt stay local. Binary collection remains under a 1.2 GB total evidence budget and the 1.4 GB per-file admission, so oversized complete setup/full packages retain compact identity metadata without an unsupported transfer. This evidence is not installer execution, installation or runtime acceptance.

Hosted source 1271e06 diagnostic result

Preservation run 38972521474, attempt 1, used exact source 1271e06b139875442f3a5850cfd2cacae2c8cfcb and installed version 0.1.171. Assembly reconstructed 19,279 Office files and proceeded through native compilation and genuine Squirrel production. The collected ownership receipt records the compiled broker SHA-256 as 7e9b00704071e0fbd9943b319122bac3bdb1729c9c30c7d8abfa5263bbb7b479 and the compiled embedding helper SHA-256 as e5d82188fc0ab63545aedf5e557928648206959c04b77e08af13c182d81b52ea. Both remain runtime-unverified.

The genuine full package measured 1,375,477,453 bytes (SHA-256 91af357c68094370843b3a79436370ad89db1bb2348001c446aa198e45dd5ba4), and the delta measured 1,316,896,276 bytes (SHA-256 12c0019c98a228d2fe8feb05be80a090a2b47761a6dd0b5c4402a9b1825ba4d5). Both now fit the unchanged 1.4 GB budget. The configured setup was 193,024 bytes (SHA-256 8b81606504e7e7fa124887288a1b820750476d2a118c02b04849ce409e4bc0a4), with a 17,230-byte PE resource directory containing FLAGS but no DATA resource. This differs from the earlier template-updater-only setup and is not assumed to have the same cause.

The root producer exited 1 at embedded package admission: Setup must contain one genuine embedded package ZIP resource. No installer execution, installation or runtime acceptance followed. The bounded diagnostic artifact retained the actual small setup, feed, previous baseline and compact output/compilation metadata. It retained hashes and sizes for the current full and delta, with no claim that their binary bytes were transferred within the evidence budget. Exact genuine-helper invocation and the setup state before post-packaging resource editing were not recorded; that boundary remains unresolved and requires new source-bound evidence rather than an unchanged retry.

Source-bound embedding observation

The invocation observer records the actual genuine helper and observer hashes, the genuine child exit code, input ZIP size/hash, and setup file and DATA resource size/hash immediately before and after genuine embedding. It writes a fixed path-free JSON record only under the producer's exact owned staging, without raw command arguments, paths or standard output. The upstream helper source and byte provenance remain unchanged. Its child exit is propagated; missing observation, nonzero exit or a resource differing from the input ZIP fails root production even if the older Squirrel driver would otherwise continue.

After the packager returns, root admission records the final configured setup's format and compares its resource identity with the genuine helper's post-embedding identity. This distinguishes a failure at genuine embedding from a resource disappearing or changing later, without guessing which later resource editor caused it. setup-embedding.json and the extended compiled-helper identities are included in bounded failure collection. Source-only instrumentation does not establish any observed outcome; the next exact-source hosted producer must supply that evidence. No post-edit bypass, format replacement, size-cap increase or runtime/installation acceptance is introduced.

Release versions

MATERIAL_BUILD_VERSION selects an explicit three-component numeric version. Otherwise a hosted GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER selects <source major>.<source minor>.<run number>. Components are bounded to 0 through 65534, and a workflow sequence is positive. Each independently numbered hosted build therefore changes the actual installed application and Squirrel package version, rather than merely changing a release tag while shipping version 0.1.0 again. Retrying the same workflow run retains its installed version. The release provenance and tag use the receipt's exact package version, and publication rejects a conflicting build/publication identity.

A local build without either input uses the source manifest version and records packageVersionSource: local-base. This is suitable for local production only. Manual publication requires an explicit MATERIAL_BUILD_VERSION, chosen strictly newer than the published installed version; publishing a locally produced base version is rejected. Keep the same version input for production and publication. Do not rewrite historical release tags or replace their packages.

Genuine delta production

Set MATERIAL_BUILD_SQUIRREL_BASELINE to a local directory containing a previous release's RELEASES and its matching full package before invoking the root installer entrypoint. Acquire those files through the project's existing trusted release route. The producer preserves the originals, rejects linked baseline paths, bounds metadata and package size, selects the newest strictly older compatible full package, and verifies its SHA-1 and byte count against RELEASES. This is transport integrity, not a publisher authenticity claim.

Hosted installer production automatically acquires a baseline when no explicit local baseline is supplied. The exact root driver uses the previously bootstrapped GitHub CLI to discover at most thirty normal releases, select an older numeric version, download its provenance, verify the exact peeled tag/source identity and compatible package version, then acquire only RELEASES and that version's full package. Asset byte counts and SHA-256 values must match the release API and provenance; the subsequent Squirrel staging also checks the feed's SHA-1. Metadata is capped at 1 MiB per file and the full package at 1.5 GB. The ignored cache preserves inputs, permits at most eight acquisition directories, and stops at the bound rather than deleting evidence. Baseline readback or integrity failures stop production; an inventory with no eligible older release records delta unavailable explicitly. Receipts retain the baseline tag/source, package identity and hashes without local paths. There is no separate workflow-only packaging command that bypasses this root producer.

The verified baseline is copied into the isolated Squirrel output directory. The pinned genuine Squirrel releasifier produces the new full and delta packages. A supplied baseline without a resulting delta fails production. Generated RELEASES entries must match each package's actual bytes and digest. The output keeps the older full package needed by that feed alongside the current packages. Publication must retain every package named by the feed.

Without a baseline the producer creates a valid full-package release and records delta.status: unavailable with its reason. It never fabricates a delta or treats that state as two-version update proof. To produce the next delta, provide the previous successful output's Squirrel directory or the corresponding downloaded release files, and choose a strictly higher installed version.

Scope and remaining evidence

No paid certificate or public trust claim is introduced. Unsigned packages can trigger unknown-publisher or SmartScreen warnings. Installation, installed launch, cross-version update, cancellation, rollback, and native runtime behavior require separate acceptance evidence. Under the fast release workflow, tests, reviews, static analysis, screenshots, installation, and runtime checks are intentionally not run. PH10-T02 remains pending its final applicable acceptance until those separately required records exist.
